original_question: For the same lattice-click model, determine the click distributions and resulting dynamical patterns in special cases such as when C is a line segment, a polygon, or a circle.
target_in_paper: Mark Levi, Problem 1, Question 3: "Analyze special cases of the segment; a polygon; a circle."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the intended open problem as Mark Levi's lattice-click model and preserves the exact three special cases singled out in the paper: a line segment, a polygon, and a circle. It also correctly interprets the task as describing the click distribution/pattern produced by the translating curve.
missing_details: To make the question stand-alone, the underlying model must be stated: one considers a curve C ⊂ R^2 together with an ε-sized square lattice.
The motion is a one-parameter translation of C, with translation parameter λ; the relevant data are the λ-values at which the translated curve contains a lattice point.
The object to analyze is the resulting set/distribution of click times (the paper also describes this as a "cloud of clicks"), not an unspecified dynamical system.
The paper records a built-in periodicity: the click cloud is periodic in λ with period ε, so one may restrict attention to λ ∈ [0, ε].
To stay paper-faithful, the problem should list exactly the three cases named in Question 3, not present them as merely illustrative examples.

The neighboring questions in the same Problem 1 ask instead about recovering the shape of C from the click data and about a possible "Fourier transform" extracting curvature-induced patterns; those should not be folded into the special-cases question.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or "for all sufficiently large m" quantifier appears in this geometric problem.
refined_question: In Mark Levi's lattice-click model, let C ⊂ R^2 be a curve and fix an ε-sized square lattice. As C moves through the given one-parameter family of translates indexed by λ, record the λ-values for which the translated curve contains a lattice point; equivalently, study the resulting cloud of clicks, viewed modulo its natural period ε (so it suffices to consider λ ∈ [0, ε]). Analyze this click set/distribution explicitly in the three special cases where C is a line segment, a polygon, or a circle.
justification: The draft clearly targets Mark Levi's Problem 1, Question 3, because the paper's exact formulation is "Analyze special cases of the segment; a polygon; a circle," and it appears immediately after the lattice-click setup. The setup defining the problem is given in the opening lines of Mark Levi's Problem 1: a curve C in R^2, an ε-sized square lattice, and clicks produced when the translated curve meets lattice points, with λ as the translation parameter. The nearby context also explains that one studies the distribution/cloud of click times and includes the periodicity observation that the click cloud has period ε, so only λ in [0, ε] needs to be considered. By contrast, Questions 1 and 2 on the same page concern shape recovery and a possible "Fourier transform" of the click cloud. The refined question therefore isolates only the special-case analysis requested in Question 3 and imports just the contextual definitions needed to make it self-contained.
